artifacts.summary: Nine-phase plan: one definition-to-theorem conversion (Limit over discrete duration orders), a sixteen-theorem frame-constraint independence matrix, a generated cross-repository citation manifest with a new freshness invariant, and a name-keyed record of the 24-definition inspection-only residue.

memory_candidates.content: A file:line citation that crosses a repository boundary is outside every gate in both repositories, and drifts silently. Observed in BimodalLogic/ProofChecker: four rows of the consuming repository's adequacy citation table drifted by exactly +38 lines and landed inside a different theorem, undetected, because the declaration-span cross-check that would have caught it (invariant C20's third assertion) has live scope over its own repository's files only. The durable remedy, which this codebase independently arrived at twice already (paper-definitions-of-record.md resolves paper anchors by \label name and re-derives hashes; theorem-index.md states 'no line numbers: cite declaration names'), is: a citation leaving a repository carries a declaration NAME and no line number, and any line-numbered view is a GENERATED manifest re-derived by the same span reader the gate uses, with a freshness assertion wired into the producing repository's own gate set so a rename or docstring sweep fails loudly at the source rather than rotting a table downstream. Generalizes to any cross-artifact citation where the citing and cited files are gated separately.
